result.solution_description: Implemented complete asynchronous stale-while-revalidate behavior while preserving the public API. The cache now distinguishes fresh, stale, and fully expired entries at the required TTL boundaries; coalesces loader tasks per key; permits independent keys to load concurrently; serves stale values immediately while launching one background refresh; tracks immutable statistics with the specified counting semantics; propagates blocking-load failures while consuming detached refresh exceptions; shields shared work from waiter cancellation; snapshots running tasks in wait_for_refreshes(); and uses per-key generations so invalidation cannot be undone by an older in-flight load or refresh. Added deterministic tests covering boundaries, same-key and cross-key concurrency, refresh and blocking failures, cancellation, wait snapshots, and invalidation races.
result.evidence: Validation command completed successfully: git diff --check and compileall produced no errors, and unittest reported all 10 focused tests passing (`Ran 10 tests in 0.014s`, `OK`). Tests include fresh/stale/expiry boundaries, per-key coalescing, concurrent different-key loads, failed background refresh preservation/counting, blocking failure propagation/retry, load and refresh invalidation races, wait_for_refreshes snapshot semantics, and cancellation of one shared-load waiter.

delegations.task: Review this proposed async SWR design for semantic edge cases and suggest a concise deterministic test matrix.
delegations.context: Single event-loop cache. get checks age: fresh < fresh_ttl; stale < fresh+stale; otherwise miss. One asyncio.Task per current key coalesces work; all tasks also tracked globally. Stale starts task and immediately returns old value. Missing/expired awaits asyncio.shield(task). Each task captures per-key generation and stores only if unchanged. invalidate increments generation, removes entry, and detaches current in-flight mapping so a subsequent get starts new work; old task remains globally tracked. Done callback consumes exception and removes mapping only by identity. Background task failures increment refresh_failures; its task retains the exception so a later expired blocking caller joining it observes failure. wait_for_refreshes snapshots global tasks and gathers shielded tasks with return_exceptions=True. Stats are incremented per specified call/start.
delegations.response:
Recommendation: make time, task completion, and scheduling explicit in tests (use a fake monotonic clock and manually controlled awaitables), and assert both returned values and state/statistics.

Deterministic matrix:

| Case | Setup/action | Expected result |
|---|---|---|
| Fresh hit | Entry age `< fresh_ttl`; call `get` | Returns cached value; no loader/task; no miss or refresh-start increment. |
| Fresh boundary | Age exactly `fresh_ttl` | Confirm whether this is stale (given `fresh` is strictly `<`); stale behavior applies. |
| Stale hit | Age in `[fresh_ttl, fresh_ttl + stale_ttl)`; loader blocked | Immediately returns old value; exactly one refresh task starts; task stores new value on success. |
| Stale upper boundary | Age exactly `fresh_ttl + stale_ttl` | Confirm it is expired/missing, not stale; caller awaits a task. |
| Expired/missing coalescing | Concurrent callers for absent/expired key | One loader/task, all callers receive its result; stats reflect the specified per-call versus per-start rules. |
| Successful blocking load | Await expired/missing `get` | New value is returned and stored with the captured generation. |
| Loader failure, blocking | Expired/missing caller joins failing task | Caller observes the exception; mapping is removed by done callback; exception is consumed without duplicate/unhandled reporting. |
| Loader failure, background | Stale refresh fails | Original stale caller still gets old value; `refresh_failures` increments once; later expired caller joining the still-current failed task observes the failure. |
| Background failure after callback | Let failed task finish, then inspect mapping/global tracking | Per-key mapping is removed only if identity still matches; task remains/removes from global tracking according to its defined lifecycle; no duplicate failure count. |
| Same-key concurrency | Multiple stale callers before completion | One refresh task and one loader invocation; every caller gets the old value promptly. |
| Different keys | Concurrent gets for distinct keys | Independent tasks and entries; no cross-key coalescing. |
| Invalidate before completion | Start load, invalidate, then complete old task | Generation changes and entry is absent; old result is not stored; subsequent get starts a new task. |
| Invalidate then reload | Start old task, invalidate, start new task, complete in both orders | New task’s result may store; old task never overwrites it, including if old completion occurs last. |
| Invalidate during stale refresh | Stale caller receives old value, then invalidates | Refresh result is discarded by generation check; next get does not treat the invalidated entry as valid. |
| Invalidate with failed old task | Detach old mapping, start replacement, fail old task | Old done callback must not remove replacement mapping; replacement remains joinable. |
| Cancellation of one waiter | Cancel a blocking caller while loader continues | Determine whether loader remains alive (shielding implies yes); other waiters still receive the result and storage occurs. |
| Cancellation of loader/task | Cancel the underlying task | Define expected exception, mapping cleanup, refresh-failure accounting, and whether subsequent get retries. |
| `wait_for_refreshes` snapshot | Snapshot while tasks A/B exist; add task C afterward | Waits only for the documented snapshot (A/B), or explicitly document otherwise; shield prevents waiter cancellation from cancelling tasks. |
| `wait_for_refreshes` failures | Snapshot includes successful and failing tasks | Completes without raising due to `return_exceptions=True`; all tasks are settled and failure handling/stats are deterministic. |
| Empty wait | No globally tracked tasks | Returns immediately. |
| Done-callback race | Old task completes after invalidation and replacement mapping exists | Identity check prevents old callback from deleting replacement. |
| Repeated gets after expiry | Failed or discarded task is complete; call again | Mapping cleanup permits a fresh attempt, unless retained failed-task semantics intentionally require retry/join behavior. |

Clarify before implementation: exact inclusive/exclusive TTL boundaries; whether `stale_ttl` can be zero or negative; loader cancellation and exception types; whether invalidation itself has stats; whether a failed background task remains mapped until a later caller or is removed immediately; global-task removal timing; behavior when the loader returns `None`; and whether clock rollback/large jumps are supported. Also test synchronous loader completion, because callback ordering can expose mapping-cleanup races.
